title: Not Yet Decided
logline: For months, a household has been going back and forth on whether one of them should go abroad for work. Agency visits, forms half-filled, evenings of the same conversation. Nobody in the house can quite say what they have decided.

object.note: Object 3 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: What replaces the heat is not certainty but something quieter; the next film stays inside that quiet, in a household that cannot settle whether someone should go abroad for work.

thread_out.thread: The question of which way to go leaves a family's evenings and becomes a real road: on unsigned dry-zone tracks, Chathura keeps stopping to ask the way.

requirements: A household currently in the middle of a genuine, unresolved decision about overseas labour migration
Willingness from every family member shown to be filmed discussing it
A realistic filming window that can hold an open-ended, possibly unresolved story

suggestions.name: A household in a district with a long-established pattern of overseas labour migration
suggestions.region: Kurunegala or Puttalam district, North Western Province
suggestions.why: A region-level suggestion only; overseas employment for work is a broadly familiar path from many parts of Sri Lanka.
suggestions.verify: A specific family currently facing this decision, and willing to be filmed, must be found and confirmed.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A choice that keeps circling without landing wears on a whole household. The texts describe a mind that cannot settle very precisely, yet they are clear that ordinary uncertainty about an unknown future is not a fault.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: තීරණයකට එන්නට නොහැකිව එකම ප්‍රශ්නය වටේ කැරකීම මුළු පවුලටම වෙහෙසක් වුවත්, නොදන්නා අනාගතයක් ගැන ඇතිවන සාමාන්‍ය අවිනිශ්චිත බව වරදක් නොවන බව ධර්මය පැහැදිලිව කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma's doubting state of mind is the sparest on its list: it lacks decision (adhimokkha), desire-to-act (chanda) and joy, and simply fails to settle. Pradeepika compares doubt to someone reaching a crossroads for the first time, worn out by not knowing which road to take. But both texts say plainly that ordinary uncertainty about unknown matters is not this unwholesome doubt (vicikicchā), which concerns the Buddha and the teaching specifically.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film sits inside the family's unfinished sentences: agency visits, forms half-filled and set aside, the same conversation returning in the evenings while daily life carries on underneath. The viewer feels the weight of not deciding without anyone doing anything dramatic, and the film ends on whatever the family actually decides, or does not.
lesson.caution: This does not mean the family's indecision is a moral failing or 'doubt' in the religious sense; the source's doubt is about the teaching, and the link here is only an analogy.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed what remains when the old heat is gone; here the heat has faded but no clarity has taken its place, and the lesson turns from anger to the tiring circle of not knowing which way to go.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
